_comment: Canonical spectral-class-to-colour cases, shared by the PHP and React renderers.
'What colour is this star?' was implemented twice -- PHP (MapRenderer::getStarColor via
getSpecClass) and React (getStarColor in src/domain/star.ts) -- and they disagreed for
roughly 460 stars. Found by audit-data on 2026-07-31; audit-parity missed it, because
parity had been comparing naming, placement, units and filtering but not rendering.
The divergences were:
- PHP strips a leading 'sd' (subdwarf) or ' d' prefix before reading the class
letter; React read character 0 blindly, so 'sdF8:' became class 's' and fell
through to white instead of the F colour.
- PHP maps R to the K colour and C/N/S to the M colour (carbon and S-type stars are
cool and red); React had no entry for any of them, so all four fell to white.
Live counts at the time: 53 stars with spect starting 'sd', 145 C, 116 N, 49 S, 103 R.
This file is the single source of truth the two renderers lacked. It is mounted into
every test container at /fixtures (see the Makefile), exactly like display-names.json.
COLOURS ARE NAMED, NOT HEXED. The two UIs deliberately use different palettes -- the
2D map uses GD's flat colours, the 3D view uses a warmer set tuned for an emissive
material on black. Pinning hex values here would force them to converge on a single
palette, which is not the goal. What must agree is the CLASSIFICATION: two stars that
map to 'red' in one renderer must map to 'red' in the other.
'white' is the fallback for anything unrecognised, including the 22,460 D-prefix white
dwarfs. Both renderers already agreed on that and it is asserted here so it stays true.

cases.why: Sirius; PHP has no explicit A branch, so it falls to white
carbon star, older R classification; shares the K colour
carbon star; cool and deeply reddened
subdwarf prefix stripped; class is F, not s
leading space then d; PHP reads index 2 for both forms
white dwarf; no entry in either renderer, falls back
Wolf-Rayet; unrecognised by both, falls back
